dod_intent_evidence: AFWERX $1.25M Direct-to-Phase-II (Jan 2024) for next-gen tactical UAS plus the 2022 USAF Phase II for HAMR base-security ISR (news section, SBIR abstract).
score_evidence: Spec-forward framing — '3.5+ hours', '800 acres in 90 minutes', '6x increase in flight time' — though tied to manning outcomes → lab_language_intensity

Strong physical fielding fluency ('austere land or maritime conditions', 'IP54 rated', 'field maintainable') but zero cyber/accreditation language: no Blue UAS, no ATO for the GCS/data link, no ITAR mention → deployment_awareness_absence
Tiny team (5-11 people) with a Jan-2024 D2P2 clock running and 'Now Shipping!' pressure to convert SBIR into program revenue → stage_pressure
No jobs data in pack → hiring_profile_skew set exactly 10 per rule

blind_spots.blind_spot: ISR-T mission with QGroundControl as the standard GCS and no TAK integration mentioned
blind_spots.operator_reality: Base defense ISR is consumed on ATAK screens in the BDOC; a feed that lives only in QGroundControl on a DesertRotor ground station is a stovepipe the security forces squadron can't task or share — the transition dies at C2 integration, not at flight performance
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Aeronautical-engineering founders (NASA-style design philosophy) optimized the air vehicle; the consumption side of the ISR product is inherited COTS

blind_spots.blind_spot: COTS PixHawk/PX4 open-source autopilot with no Blue UAS or NDAA-compliance claim anywhere
blind_spots.operator_reality: Group 1/2 UAS procurement for base security now gates on Blue UAS listing and data-link cybersecurity; without it, units legally can't buy the aircraft no matter how well it flies — the exact demo-to-fielded wall
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Open-source flight stack was the fast prototyping path; certification is a compliance program a 6-person company hasn't staffed
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Autopilot Hardware | PixHawk Cube Blue … Autopilot Software | PX4

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Field maintainable' hybrid gasoline engine with no training or sustainment chain described
blind_spots.operator_reality: A combustion engine at an austere OCONUS site means fuel logistics, spark plugs, vibration-mount spares, and an E-5 with 20 minutes of training doing small-engine maintenance in dust — 'line replaceable components' only helps if the spares pipeline and the training pipeline exist
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Claims come from engineering test experience ('this test plot confirms…negligible vibration'), not from a fielded sustainment program
blind_spots.evidence_quote: it is rapidly setup (less than 5 minutes), durable (IP54 rated), and field maintainable.

opener_hook: HAMR ships with PX4 and QGroundControl as its standard stack for base-security ISR-T, and no Blue UAS listing or TAK integration appears anywhere on flyaac.com.
what_they_do: 11-person veteran-owned Hampton, VA shop building HAMR, a hybrid gas-electric multirotor drone with 3.5-hour endurance for base perimeter security and maritime ISR, now shipping and running on AFWERX Phase II money.
